candidates.exact_span: The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of NOEC and the 95% confidence threshold could change whether a WET result is treated as meeting or exceeding an applicable toxicity-based discharge limit.

candidates.exact_span: Chronic lethal test failure is defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what counts as a statistically significant lethal effect at or below the critical dilution could change whether a reported WET result is classified as a limit exceedance.

candidates.exact_span: Chronic sub-lethal test failure is defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant sub-lethal effect (i.e., growth or reproduction) at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretation of sub-lethal significance at or below the critical dilution could change whether growth or reproduction endpoints trigger a compliance exceedance.
